title: Problem 04
markdown:
### Problem
Determine all pairs $(d, r)$ of positive integers with the property that when each of the numbers 904, 1259 and 2040 is divided by $d$, the same remainder $r$ (with $0 < r < d$) occurs.

### Solution (adapted from the official solution)
Let $a, b, c \in \mathbb{Z}$.

$$
\begin{aligned}
904 &= ad + r \\
1259 &= bd + r \qquad 0 < r < d \\
2040 &= cd + r
\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}
1259 - 904 &= (b - a)d = 355 \\
2040 - 1259 &= (c - b)d = 781
\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\therefore\quad d \mid 355, \qquad d \mid 781
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}
781 &= 2(355) + 71 \\
355 &= 5(71) + 0
\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\therefore\quad \gcd(355, 781) = 71
$$

$$
\therefore\quad d \mid 71 \implies d \in \{1, 71\}
$$

$$
0 < r < d \implies d > 1 \implies d = 71
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}
904 &= 12(71) + 52 \\
1259 &= 17(71) + 52 \\
2040 &= 28(71) + 52
\end{aligned}
$$

$$
0 < 52 < 71
$$

$$
(d, r) = (71, 52)
$$

### Conceptual Explanation
When numbers have equal remainder mod $d$, $d$ must divide their pairwise differences: $d \mid \gcd(1259 - 904, 2040 - 1259) = \gcd(355, 781) = 71$ via [Euclidean algorithm](#node/node-modular-arithmetic/sec-modular-arithmetic-core). Since 71 is prime and $d > 1$, $d = 71$. Dividing 904 by 71 gives quotient 12 and remainder 52.

### Key Technique
Equal remainder condition implies $d \mid \gcd(x - y, y - z)$; [Euclidean algorithm](#node/node-modular-arithmetic/sec-modular-arithmetic-core) on pairwise differences.
